KEY MESSAGE 1...Mainly dry conditions through Sunday with the 
exception of an isolated shower or storm today. Unsettled weather 
arrives Sunday night.

Day Cloud Phase satellite imagery shows development of shallow 
cumulus this afternoon with a few isolated showers driven by 
the diurnal heating. Expect any showers to diminish around 
sunset. Quiet weather overnight with weak high pressure 
overhead. Moisture advects in within the southerly flow tonight 
similar to last night. Model soundings show a signal for 
moisture in the low levels under an inversion with the strongest
signal for the south coast and Cape/Islands. This will increase
the potential for stratus and perhaps some fog. HREF has shown 
potential for the stratus to push northward after midnight 
although there is lower confidence how far north it extends. 
Patch fog is also possible in the CT Valley overnight. 

Similar pattern for Sunday with the mid-level ridge and surface high 
offshore as a shortwave trough to the west of the region. Weak high 
pressure stays put over the area keeping conditions mainly dry. 
Can't rule out an isolated shower or storm in the afternoon, mainly 
in western MA. High temperatures range in the low to mid 80s for 
most with southerly winds. Skies will be mainly cloudy. 

A low pressure system moves through the Ohio Valley as the mid-level 
trough pushes further east across western southern New England 
Sunday night. An accompanying LLJ pushes northward into the 
region. This will help advect in a plume of above normal 
moisture into the region ahead of the approaching trough. A mix 
of isentropic lift and jet dynamics will provide synoptic 
support for rain developing Sunday night. There is a signal for 
marginal instability which may support a few embedded moderate 
showers or brief downpours in localized areas with the higher 
risk for western MA/CT. The higher risk for the heavier rainfall
will be Monday (see next key message). 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Cold front brings showers and thunderstorms with heavy rain 
Monday. Street flooding is possible. A brief break on Tuesday before 
turning active and unsettled again Wednesday.

Still monitoring the potential for heavy rain into the early and 
possibly into the middle portion of next week. This rain and 
embedded thunderstorms looks to be forced by an injection of 
subtropical moisture on SWly low-level jet maxima of upwards of 45 
kt Monday, ahead of an anomalously strong mid-level low stalling 
over the lower OH Valley Monday and remaining more-or-less in place 
into early next week. This strong meridional flow of air brings 
precipitable water values to 2-2.25", corresponding to anomalies 
which are 2 to 2.5 standard deviations above normal! A slow-moving 
south-to-north surface cold frontal boundary will interact with this 
subtropical moisture plume and favor rounds of showers and 
thunderstorms. Monday looks to be a washout with moderate (40-60%) 
model-ensemble probabilities of 24-hr rainfall totals at/over 
1", with very low (<10%) chances of 24-hr rain totals at/over 
over 2". Will have to watch for possible street and poor 
drainage flooding in heavy downpours, as well as rises on 
rivers, creeks and streams as USGS streamflow data over the last
7 days (e.g. coming out of the very wet stretch we've had of 
late) show most rivers running above- to well-above normal. 
WPC's excessive rainfall outlook shows as much as a Level 2 of 4
(Slight) Risk for Excessive Rainfall for Monday. While not a 
zero-risk, severe weather potential looks to be a more limited, 
secondary risk in the form of water-loaded downdrafts given the 
juiced airmass. 

It looks like on Tuesday that the northern end of the frontal 
boundary shifts the axis of highest PWAT values offshore, and allows 
for weak subsidence to return - put another way, it looks like 
Tuesday is a general minimum in rain chances, but it's still 
unsettled as the mid-level low to our south could still allow for 
northward-moving showers and storms in the northern Mid-Atlantic to 
clip portions of western Southern New England. A better chance for 
another round of showers and storms mainly into western/central 
Southern New England returns by Wednesday. All told a pretty muggy 
and unsettled weather pattern with several opportunities for 
showers and storms. 

Temperatures should run above normal, especially with regard to the 
low temps in a humid, muggy airmass. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Still unsettled late in the week with periods of 
showers and storms. 

The mid-level low over the Ohio Valley weakens and washes out into 
Thursday. Unfortunately an active northern stream portion of the jet 
continues, so it still ends up looking unsettled with showers/storms
